behaviors.text: A visitor can create an account with an email address and a password.
A registered user can sign in with correct credentials, and is refused with incorrect ones.
A signed-in user can sign out, after which their session no longer authenticates them.
A session persists across requests: the signed-in user can be read back from the session cookie.
Protected routes reject unauthenticated requests before running any business logic.

tests.description: Registering with a fresh email creates an account and opens a session.
Correct credentials are accepted and produce a session cookie.
An incorrect password is rejected. This is the test that fails if hashing was reimplemented wrongly.
The session cookie issued at login identifies the same user on a later request.
After logout the previously valid session no longer authenticates.
A protected route rejects a request carrying no session.
A session issued before the application restarts is still honoured after it (durable session storage).
